saddlebag fill
  Type a stored value into a field of an open browser page over the DevTools protocol.
  runs: saddlebag fill {name} --field {field} --selector {selector} --url-contains {url_contains} --cdp {cdp} [--json]
  body: FillArgs
  0 → lines of text: the number of characters typed, the selector and the page's URL
  1 → Stderr: the store cannot be reached, no such secret, the field is unknown or holds nothing, or the browser is not reachable
  2 → Stderr: the selector is left out
  carries: RunFill
    refuses 2 'usage: saddlebag fill [-h] [--field FIELD] --selector CSS\n                      [--url-contains TEXT] [--cdp URL] [--min-seconds N]\n                      [--json]\n                      name\nsaddlebag fill: error: the following arguments are required: --selector'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no saddlebag daemon on <sandbox>/run/saddlebag.sock: start one with `saddlebag serve`'
      why: a preference for the daemon sends every verb to its socket, and nothing listens there.
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no such secret: {name}'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: unknown field {field_repr}: expected one of username, password, totp or meta.<key>'
    refuses 1 "saddlebag: invalid metadata key {key_repr}: use letters, digits, '_' and '-', with no '.' or '='"
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {name} has no {named_field}. Store one with: saddlebag secret set {name} --field {named_field}'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {name} has no username.'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {name} has no {named_field}. Set one with: saddlebag secret meta {name} {key}=...'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: refusing to send a secret to non-loopback CDP endpoint {cdp_repr}. A DevTools port grants full control of the browser and is never authenticated; saddlebag will only talk to one on this machine.'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no browser answering at {cdp}: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>. Start one with --remote-debugging-port, e.g. `chromium --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=/tmp/qa-profile`'
      why: the book points fill at a loopback port nothing listens on, so it plays the refusal and never a fill.

saddlebag exec --
  Run a command with secrets in its environment and mask their values in what it prints.
  runs: saddlebag exec --tag {tag} --env {env} -- {run} {show}
  body: ExecArgs
  0 → lines of text: what the command printed, a stored value masked
  1 → Stderr: the store cannot be reached, a secret or its value is missing, or the command itself exited 1
  2 → Stderr: no command, nothing to fill, or a malformed binding or tag
  127 → Stderr: the program does not exist
  carries: RunExec
    refuses 2 'saddlebag: exec needs a command after --'
    refuses 2 'saddlebag: exec needs at least one --tag or --env'
    refuses 2 'saddlebag: invalid --env {bad_binding}: expected VAR=NAME or VAR=NAME[.field|.meta.key]'
    refuses 2 'saddlebag: invalid tag {bad_tag}: expected key=value'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no saddlebag daemon on <sandbox>/run/saddlebag.sock: start one with `saddlebag serve`'
      why: a preference for the daemon sends every verb to its socket, and nothing listens there.
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no secret carries all of those tags'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: acme has no password. Store one with: saddlebag secret set acme --field password'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: beta has no password. Store one with: saddlebag secret set beta --field password'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: invalid environment variable name {binding_var}'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: no such secret: {binding_name}'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: unknown field {binding_field_repr}: expected one of username, password, totp or meta.<key>'
    refuses 1 "saddlebag: invalid metadata key {binding_key_repr}: use letters, digits, '_' and '-', with no '.' or '='"
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {binding_name} has no {binding_field}. Store one with: saddlebag secret set {binding_name} --field {binding_field}'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {binding_name} has no username.'
    refuses 1 'saddlebag: {binding_name} has no {binding_field}. Set one with: saddlebag secret meta {binding_name} {binding_key}=...'
    refuses 127 'saddlebag: cannot run {run}: No such file or directory'
      why: the command is run after the secrets are resolved, so a missing program is the last thing exec reports.
    refuses 1 ''
      why: printenv exits 1 for a variable the command was not handed, and exec passes the child's exit code through.

KeepALogin\nA person registers the acme login with its username, variable, tags and metadata, stores its password,\n    reads the inventory, tags and untags it, adds and drops metadata, clears the password and removes the login.

RunWithSecrets
A person registers the acme and beta logins and stores a password for each and a TOTP seed for acme. They run
    a program with a login's password in its environment by name and by tag, and see a value of eight characters or
    more masked in what it prints, a shorter one left as it is, and the username and metadata in the clear. They are
    refused a command with nothing to fill, a malformed binding or tag, a tag nobody carries, an unknown secret, a field
    the secret lacks, a variable the program was not handed and a program that does not exist.

ReadADotenv
A person reads the app's dotenv without seeing a secret. With an empty store, the token and the credentialed
    URL are masked by their shapes and the registered password is a literal. Once the acme login is registered its
    variable is secret, and once its password is stored the same value is secret by what it holds. They change a
    literal and add a new one, are refused a key or value that is secret, a key that is not a name and a value on
    two lines, and import two keys of the file as secrets of their own.

MoveAStore
A person loads an export from another machine into the store and is refused a file that is missing, is not
    JSON or is no export. The second load is refused because its secret is already there, and succeeds with --replace.
    Export is refused for a name that does not end in .saddlebag.json, and from any command run without a terminal.

GuardTheAgents
A person registers the guard in a project's settings and in their own, once in a project that already has
    settings of its own. The guard then refuses an agent action that reads a dotenv, a key file or an export and says
    how to get the same thing, lets the examples, the other actions and `saddlebag exec` through, and ignores what is no
    JSON. A bare `saddlebag guard`, and an install that names neither or both scopes, are refused.

ReachAScreen
A person asks saddlebag to type the acme login into a browser page and an Android field, and is told what
    stands in the way: no such secret, nothing stored under the field, a selector left out, a browser on another host,
    no browser listening and no adb. They keep a Vault token for the daemon and are refused a daemon with no address or
    no token.

ChooseARoute
A person's home config prefers the daemon, though none runs, and every verb that reaches the store is refused
    with where it looked. They switch the preference to the keyring and the store answers again. They leave a Vault
    token in their home and doctor warns of it.
- **empty**: no secret is stored. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.

- **registered**: 'acme' is created and holds no value. Reached by: saddlebag secret create acme --username ana --description 'the acme login' --var ACME_PW --tag env=ci --tag team=a --meta realm=prod.

- **stocked**: 'acme' holds a password and a TOTP seed and 'beta' holds a password. Reached by: saddlebag secret create acme --username ana --description 'the acme login' --var ACME_PW --tag env=ci --tag team=a --meta realm=prod; saddlebag secret set acme < 'hunter2hunter2'; saddlebag secret set acme --field totp < 'JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP'; saddlebag secret create beta --var BETA_PW --tag env=ci --tag team=b; saddlebag secret set beta < 'short'.
- **daemon-preferred**: the home config prefers the daemon and none runs. Reached by: ChooseDaemon.

elements: EnvShow, EnvKeys, EnvClassify, EnvSet, EnvImport
A dotenv line is secret when its value is a stored password or seed (held-value), its key is the variable of a
registered secret (registered-var), or its shape says so: a key named like a credential, a vendor token, a URL with a
password in it (saddlebag/saddlebag/verbs.py, verb_classify, and shapes.py). The rules are tried in that order, so the
same ACME_PW line is a literal in an empty store, secret by its variable once acme is registered, and secret by its value
once acme holds the password.
The dotenv the book gives every world is `app.env`. Its lines are the strings the watch looks for, so the file's
rows say which lines it holds. `env set` writes a literal in place or at the end, and refuses a key or a value that is
secret with exit 2 (cmd_env_set).

`list` and the catalogue say which of a secret's two values exist (`fields`) and never carry one
(saddlebag/saddlebag/models.py, Secret.to_dict). The only command that hands a value to a process is `exec`, so the

elements: Tags, TagSecret, UntagSecret, Meta, Unmeta
A tag is a key and a value, and a secret carries a set of them, so tagging twice with one pair keeps one and untagging a pair
the secret lacks does nothing (saddlebag/saddlebag/verbs.py, verb_tag and verb_untag). `list` and `tags` print them

that is not key=value is refused by the command line with exit 2, before any request is made (cmd_tag, cmd_meta).

`saddlebag serve` runs until a signal, and past its checks it needs a reachable Vault. The book plays the checks that
end it: no address, no token on stdin, and keeping a token in the keyring (cmd_serve, custody.py). A valid token with an
address reaches a Vault the sandbox lacks, and the app then dies with a traceback (DISAGREEMENTS 2), so no claim names it.

verb is sent to the daemon's socket, and with none listening each says where it looked. The book plays that refusal and
never a served verb.

saddlebag/saddlebag/lookup.py is the call a Python program makes to read one secret's value in process (secret_value). No command
a person types reaches it, and the book is the model of the command line, so the file is ignored. It sends the same `env` request

elements: SecretRecord, Create, SetValue, Doctor
saddlebag keeps a secret's value in the OS keyring and its record in a catalogue file under the state directory
(saddlebag/saddlebag/keyring_store.py, catalogue.py). It refuses any keyring that is not the Secret Service or the macOS
Keychain, so a sandbox with no desktop session answers every verb with "no OS keyring on this session"
(keyring_store.py, open_door).
The book therefore starts a message bus and gnome-keyring-daemon for each world, unlocks the login keyring, and
hands the sandbox the bus address. The catalogue sits under the sandbox's home, so a world holds its own records, and
the keyring is thrown away with the world, so no value outlives it. The sandbox runs the real app against a real
keyring and no stand-in for either.

machine may have one, and `type` would then reach a device the claim never arranged.
story: none
elements: Doctor, Fill, GuardInstall, ChooseDaemon
Programs print absolute paths, and a sandbox is a new directory for every world. The surface writes the sandbox path
as <sandbox> in everything the program printed, so a message built from a path is the same text in every world and the
rules quote it. The daemon's socket is the run directory's saddlebag.sock (saddlebag/saddlebag/sockets.py,
socket_path), and the guard installs into the sandbox's `.claude` or the home's.
story: none
elements: Look, FileRecord
After every step the run reads what the store holds with `saddlebag list --json`, which names each secret, which of its
two values exist and never a value, and the files of the sandbox it watches: the home config's route, the dotenv, the
export files, the guard's settings and the Vault token file. A file's row lists which of the strings the book declares
for it the file holds (saddlebag/saddlebag/dotenv.py, guard.py, preference.py).
story: none
elements: Version
`--version` prints the version of the installed stablemate-saddlebag distribution (saddlebag/saddlebag/cli.py,
build_parser). The book plays it for the line's shape and the number the pyproject names, and a release moves the number.
